# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 - Summary

## Economic Vision

The Conservatives present their manifesto as a continuation of economic recovery following COVID-19 and the Ukraine crisis. They highlight falling inflation (from 11.1% to 2.3%), rising real wages, and returning growth as evidence their plan is working. The party commits to reducing borrowing and debt while maintaining fiscal rules.

## Key Tax Pledges

The centrepiece is cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing a £1,350 annual saving for average workers. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The new "Triple Lock Plus" guarantees both State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowances rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. Child Benefit reforms would move to a household basis, with families retaining benefits until combined income reaches £120,000.

## Immigration and Borders

The party pledges to introduce a legally binding cap on migration, with numbers falling annually. They commit to continuing Rwanda deportation flights and reforming international asylum rules. A "UK Connection" test for social housing would prioritise those with established ties to the country.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, described as the largest sustained increase since the Cold War. The manifesto emphasises continued support for Ukraine and maintaining the nuclear deterrent. A new Veterans' Bill would enshrine veterans' rights in law.

## Public Services

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with commitments to recruit 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. The party promises 8,000 additional neighbourhood police officers and continued prison expansion. Mental health support would expand to 100% of schools by 2030.

## Housing and Planning

The target is 1.6 million new homes, focusing on brownfield development and urban regeneration. First-time buyers would benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. The Green Belt would remain protected from "uncontrolled development."

## Energy and Environment

The party commits to net zero by 2050 through a "pragmatic" approach, including annual North Sea oil and gas licensing rounds, trebling offshore wind capacity, and expanding nuclear power with Small Modular Reactors. They guarantee no new green levies on household bills.

## Young People

A mandatory National Service programme would offer 18-year-olds either military placements or community volunteering. Education reforms include the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education and 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing poor-quality university courses.
